summary: Yakima County, WA summit cabin built 1923, staffed in the 1920s, destroyed in 1961; no source describes what remains on the summit today.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin on the summit
facts.status_note: Cabin destroyed in 1961; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit.

access.note: Reached on foot by a trail from the Mt. Aix trailhead on Bumping Lake Road; no closure or permit appears in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Willhite lists 6 miles with 4,200 feet of gain; the last few miles of road are rocky but passable by regular cars

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cabin was destroyed by fire in 1961. firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed in 1961 and name no cause. All three put the loss in 1961.
firelookout.com gives the lookout elevation as 7776 ft (about 2370 m), the record's figure. Willhite gives the summit as 7,766 ft. The record is kept as is.

sources.title: Mount Aix Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register

notes_for_editor: History is consistent across sources: built 1923, destroyed 1961. Only the register says the loss was a fire. The record's access 'unknown' is set to public from Willhite's hiking route in the wilderness; no source states a public-access rule. No source describes the summit today. The 1961 benchmark detail is from Willhite and refers to the west wall of the cabin at that time.
